subject.title: [Feature]: Optional session activity watchdog and alerts (blocked by #39127)

question: Should OpenClaw core own a built-in session activity watchdog and operator alerting surface after the sessions.activity API lands, or should core expose activity/diagnostic signals for plugins and dashboards to consume?
rationale: The request adds new core feature, config, delivery, privacy, UI/operator, and optional model-call behavior rather than repairing an existing contract, so automation cannot choose the product boundary safely.

options.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
options.body: Keep #39141 open as the downstream product/design item once #39127 settles the canonical sessions.activity contract.

options.title: Route alerting to plugins or dashboards
options.body: Close or redirect this if maintainers want core to expose activity and diagnostics only while external or plugin-owned surfaces handle alert delivery.

options.title: Defer watchdog scope
options.body: Leave the issue parked until #39127 or an equivalent activity stream lands and real operator usage clarifies the minimum alerting surface.

recommendation.title: Design core watchdog after activity API
recommendation.body: Keep #39141 open as the downstream product/design item once #39127 settles the canonical sessions.activity contract.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily a product/API boundary call across gateway sessions and Control UI ergonomics, where recent history shows active ownership signals.
